pages.text: "Oh, it will not move!" Pipo pulled a hay cart before the shed. It would not budge. Quick-stepping Mr. Horse easily pulled it inside.
Pipo plopped down. "He is big and strong... I am small, so I cannot do anything." He wanted to pull the cart too. Shoulders drooping, he fiddled with his scarf tip.
Then a thin baa came from the shed. A lamb had got into a narrow gap underneath and could not escape. Mr. Horse hurried to reach in, but his big hand could not fit far enough.
Mom ran over. "You are too big, Mr. Horse. Pipo, will you try?" Pipo sniffled. "But I am small..." Mom cradled his cheeks. "Small is why you can. Small, but still Pipo!"
Pipo lay flat and slipped his little hand into the gap. It reached where the big hand could not. Inside, the lamb trembled.
He gently pulled it out and held it close. "Out!" The lamb bleated in his arms. Mr. Horse opened his eyes wide. "Pipo reached where I could not!"
Mom patted Pipo's shoulders. "Big is part of Mr. Horse, small is part of Pipo." His eyes sparkled wide. "Small, but still Pipo!" The lamb leaned on his leg.
Pipo set it down and crouched before the shed, hands at his chest. His drooping shoulders straightened. Beside him, Mr. Horse clapped his big hands.
Mr. Horse pulled the cart, and Pipo carried the lamb beside him into the shed. "One, big jobs for big Mr. Horse! Two, small jobs for small Pipo! Three, together we can do it all!" Pipo added.
As sheep entered the pen, Pipo leaned against Mr. Horse's leg, still holding the lamb. Small ones had things they did well too. Looking up and smiling, he said, "Small, but still Pipo!"
